successors.note: Bavaria gave it up in 1805 for Tyrol and Ferdinand III of Tuscany received it, raised to the Grand Duchy of Würzburg on 30 September 1806 (Cliopatria grand-duchy-of-wurzburg, 1806-1814, eu-20); Bavaria annexed it again in 1814.

correction.text: the prince-bishopric of Würzburg (Lower Franconia), a stand-in circle

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Würzburg row; the lands sit in Holy Roman Empire Minor States). The pages opened give no area, no boundary and no territorial change at all (the Prince-Bishopric page 'does not mention' Schweinfurt, Kitzingen, Henneberg, Wertheim, Königshofen or Karlstadt); the shape is a 40 km circle at Würzburg (about 5,000 km2), a stand-in for the Hochstift on both banks of the Main. The Bamberg page gives 3,580 km2 for its neighbour, which suggests the order of magnitude. Soft.

ledger.note: 1168: the bishop becomes a prince. Infobox 'Raised to prince-bishopric: 1168'; 'the bishop was formally ceded the ducal rights in Eastern Franconia' (Herold von Hochheim, 1165-70, the first prince-bishop). The page gives no territory.

region.text: the bishop's lands round Würzburg and the ducal rights in Eastern Franconia

ledger.note: 1633: Sweden gives the bishoprics to Bernhard of Saxe-Weimar. 'In this year he was granted the former Bishoprics of Würzburg and Bamberg, being granted the title of Duke of Franconia' (a claim tagged '[citation needed]' on the page). When Swedish troops took Würzburg (1631 or 1632) is not on any page opened.

region.text: the former Bishopric of Würzburg, held as the Swedish-backed Duchy of Franconia

ledger.note: 1634: 'But in 1634 Bernard suffered a great defeat at Nördlingen'; 'Würzburg having been lost in the debacle of 1634.' The prince-bishops return. The page gives no month.

25 February 1803: the bishopric ends. Infobox 'Secularised and annexed by Bavaria: 25 February 1803'; the Grand Duchy page: 'the Bishopric of Würzburg was secularized in 1803 and granted to the Electorate of Bavaria'. Georg Karl von Fechenbach was the last prince-bishop.

wars.name: Swedish Franconia in the Thirty Years' War
wars.outcome: Bernhard of Saxe-Weimar held the Bishoprics of Würzburg and Bamberg as Duke of Franconia from 1633 and lost Würzburg after Nördlingen in 1634.
wars.note: The war span uses the Bamberg page's 1631 flight of the bishop; the Würzburg page does not mention the occupation.

certainty.note: The pages give no boundary, area or territorial change; the circle is a stand-in.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 for batch eu-09-x (4 pages; budget 5). New state: Cliopatria has no Würzburg row before the Grand Duchy of Würzburg (1806-1814).

THIN PAGES. The Prince-Bishopric page gives dates but no territory (no area, no towns, no acquisitions or losses); the Grand Duchy page gives no area either, only that Schweinfurt was added in 1810. The 40 km circle at Würzburg (9.93E 49.79N) is therefore a stand-in, not a reading of the page. Gazetteer has the place 'Würzburg'.

NOT SETTLED. (1) Area and boundary. (2) The ducal title: infobox 1441, text 1442. (3) The Swedish occupation: the 1633 grant is on the Bernhard page ('citation needed'); the Swedish capture of Würzburg (1631 or 1632) and the exact end are not on pages opened. (4) 1802: Bavarian occupation of the bishopric is on the Bamberg page; the Würzburg page does not date it. (5) The Würzburg territory of 1803-1805 (Bavarian), 1806-1814 (Grand Duchy, Ferdinand III) is in Cliopatria's Grand Duchy row and duchy-of-bavaria.

COUNTERPARTS NEEDING DOSSIERS: grand-duchy-of-wurzburg exists in Cliopatria (eu-20); county-of-henneberg (to 1583), county-of-wertheim.
